title: World Geography Challenge
seoDescription: Take a 90-question World Geography Challenge covering capitals, countries, continents, landmarks, rivers, deserts, maps, and regions.
pageTitle: Only 9% Can Pass This World Geography Challenge
summary: From capitals and continents to rivers, borders, landmarks, and regions, see how sharp your world geography really is.

homepage.title: Can You Pass This World Geography Challenge?
homepage.summary: From capitals and continents to rivers, borders, landmarks, and regions, see how sharp your world geography really is.

footer.aboutText: This World Geography Challenge is designed for entertainment and self-testing. It is not an official geography exam, school assessment, travel qualification, or professional evaluation. The quiz uses broad world-geography questions and simplified explanations.

landing.quickStartText: The first questions look easy. The later rounds reveal how well you really know the world map.

profiles.copy: Excellent world geography knowledge across capitals, regions, landmarks, and physical features. Your strongest area was {stage}.

stageGroups.title: World Geography Warm Up
stageGroups.encouragement: Warm up complete. The next round moves deeper into countries and continents.

questions.prompt: What is the capital of Canada?
questions.explanation: Ottawa is the capital city of Canada.

questions.prompt: The Great Barrier Reef is off the coast of which country?
questions.explanation: The Great Barrier Reef is off the northeast coast of Australia.

questions.prompt: How many continents are commonly counted on Earth?
questions.explanation: Most geography models count seven continents.

questions.prompt: Which country is the largest in the world by land area?
questions.explanation: Russia is the largest country by land area.

questions.prompt: The Amazon Rainforest is mostly located in which country?
questions.explanation: Most of the Amazon Rainforest is in Brazil.

questions.prompt: Mount Fuji is an iconic mountain in which country?
questions.explanation: Mount Fuji is in Japan.

questions.prompt: The Eiffel Tower is in which city?
questions.explanation: The Eiffel Tower is in Paris, France.

questions.prompt: Which desert is the largest desert on Earth?
questions.explanation: The Antarctic Desert is the largest desert by area.

questions.prompt: Which imaginary line divides Earth into Northern and Southern Hemispheres?
questions.explanation: The Equator divides Earth into Northern and Southern Hemispheres.

stageGroups.title: Continents And Countries
stageGroups.encouragement: Nice progress. Now the challenge turns toward capital cities.

questions.prompt: Which country has Portuguese as its official language?
questions.explanation: Brazil uses Portuguese as its official language.

questions.prompt: Which country has the largest population?
questions.explanation: India is currently the world's most populous country.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries is in Southeast Asia?
questions.explanation: Thailand is in Southeast Asia.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries is completely landlocked?
questions.explanation: Switzerland has no coastline.

questions.prompt: Which country is made up of more than 17,000 islands?
questions.explanation: Indonesia is an archipelagic country with more than 17,000 islands.

questions.prompt: Which continent is home to the Andes Mountains?
questions.explanation: The Andes run along western South America.

questions.prompt: Which country is shaped like a boot on many maps?
questions.explanation: Italy is often recognized by its boot-like shape.

questions.prompt: Which continent is Madagascar part of?
questions.explanation: Madagascar is an island country off the coast of Africa.

questions.prompt: Which country is located at the southern tip of Africa?
questions.explanation: South Africa is at the southern tip of the African continent.

stageGroups.title: Capital Cities And Map Clues
stageGroups.encouragement: City and map clues cleared. Next up: famous landmarks and places.

questions.prompt: Which capital city lies furthest south?
questions.explanation: Buenos Aires is farther south than Ottawa, Tokyo, and Cairo.

questions.prompt: Which country borders both France and Germany?
questions.explanation: Switzerland borders both France and Germany.

questions.prompt: Which city does not belong in Europe?
questions.explanation: Seoul is in Asia, while the other cities are in Europe.

questions.prompt: Which capital city is closest to the Equator?
questions.explanation: Quito, the capital of Ecuador, is very close to the Equator.

questions.prompt: Which country comes first alphabetically?
questions.explanation: Madagascar comes before Malaysia, Mexico, and Morocco alphabetically.

questions.prompt: Which landmark is closest to the Equator?
questions.explanation: Machu Picchu is much closer to the Equator than the other landmarks listed.

questions.prompt: What is the capital of Egypt?
questions.explanation: Cairo is the capital of Egypt.

questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Australia?
questions.explanation: Canberra is the capital of Australia.

questions.prompt: Which place is furthest north?
questions.explanation: Berlin is farther north than Cairo, Nairobi, and Buenos Aires.

stageGroups.title: Landmarks And Places
stageGroups.encouragement: Landmarks handled. The next round moves into rivers, seas, and deserts.

questions.prompt: The Taj Mahal is located in which country?
questions.explanation: The Taj Mahal is in India.

questions.prompt: In which country can you visit Machu Picchu?
questions.explanation: Machu Picchu is in Peru.

questions.prompt: The Statue of Liberty was a gift from which country?
questions.explanation: The Statue of Liberty was a gift from France.

questions.prompt: Which city is famous for canals instead of many streets?
questions.explanation: Venice is famous for its canals.

questions.prompt: What country is home to the ancient city of Petra?
questions.explanation: Petra is in Jordan.

questions.prompt: Which country is home to Christ the Redeemer?
questions.explanation: Christ the Redeemer overlooks Rio de Janeiro in Brazil.

questions.prompt: Which country is famous for the Great Wall?
questions.explanation: The Great Wall is in China.

questions.prompt: Which African country is famous for the Pyramids of Giza?
questions.explanation: The Pyramids of Giza are in Egypt.

questions.prompt: Which country is home to the Colosseum?
questions.explanation: The Colosseum is in Rome, Italy.

stageGroups.title: Rivers Seas And Deserts
stageGroups.encouragement: Physical geography is heating up. Next come mountains, islands, and borders.

questions.prompt: The Panama Canal connects which two oceans?
questions.explanation: The Panama Canal connects the Atlantic and Pacific Oceans.

questions.prompt: What body of water separates the United Kingdom from mainland Europe?
questions.explanation: The English Channel separates the United Kingdom from mainland Europe.

questions.prompt: Which ocean lies between Africa and Australia?
questions.explanation: The Indian Ocean lies between Africa and Australia.

questions.prompt: What is the world's highest waterfall?
questions.explanation: Angel Falls in Venezuela is the world's highest uninterrupted waterfall.

questions.prompt: Which African lake is the largest by area?
questions.explanation: Lake Victoria is Africa's largest lake by surface area.

questions.prompt: Which river flows through London?
questions.explanation: The River Thames flows through London.

questions.prompt: Which continent is home to the Sahara Desert?
questions.explanation: The Sahara Desert is in northern Africa.

questions.prompt: Which ocean is generally the warmest?
questions.explanation: The Indian Ocean is generally the warmest ocean.

questions.prompt: Which river runs through Egypt?
questions.explanation: The Nile River runs through Egypt.

stageGroups.title: Mountains Islands And Borders
stageGroups.encouragement: Good work. Now the quiz shifts into map sense and world regions.

questions.prompt: Which mountain range separates Europe from Asia?
questions.explanation: The Ural Mountains are commonly used as part of the boundary between Europe and Asia.

questions.prompt: Which country lies directly south of the United States?
questions.explanation: Mexico lies directly south of the United States.

questions.prompt: What is the tallest mountain in North America?
questions.explanation: Denali is the tallest mountain in North America.

questions.prompt: What natural feature separates France from Spain?
questions.explanation: The Pyrenees form a natural boundary between France and Spain.

questions.prompt: Which country shares the longest international border with the United States?
questions.explanation: Canada shares the longest international border with the United States.

questions.prompt: Which of these is an island nation?
questions.explanation: The United Kingdom is an island nation.

questions.prompt: Which country is located directly west of India?
questions.explanation: Pakistan lies directly west of India.

questions.prompt: Which country is across the Tasman Sea from Australia?
questions.explanation: New Zealand lies across the Tasman Sea from Australia.

questions.prompt: Which large island lies southeast of mainland Africa?
questions.explanation: Madagascar lies southeast of mainland Africa.

stageGroups.title: Maps And Regions
stageGroups.encouragement: Map round complete. Next comes population, culture, and world features.

questions.prompt: Which line divides Earth into Eastern and Western Hemispheres?
questions.explanation: The Prime Meridian is the 0 degree longitude line.

questions.prompt: Which of these is a continent?
questions.explanation: Africa is a continent.

questions.prompt: What is the only continent with no permanent human population?
questions.explanation: Antarctica has research stations but no permanent human population.

questions.prompt: What is the southernmost continent on Earth?
questions.explanation: Antarctica is the southernmost continent.

questions.prompt: Which city is often described as being on two continents?
questions.explanation: Istanbul spans areas on both the European and Asian sides of the Bosporus.

questions.prompt: What is the name of the peninsula where Saudi Arabia is located?
questions.explanation: Saudi Arabia is on the Arabian Peninsula.

questions.prompt: Which two continents are mostly in the Western Hemisphere?
questions.explanation: North America and South America are mostly in the Western Hemisphere.

questions.prompt: Which continent has the most countries?
questions.explanation: Africa has the most internationally recognized countries of any continent.

questions.prompt: Which large sea lies between Europe and Africa?
questions.explanation: The Mediterranean Sea lies between Europe and Africa.

stageGroups.title: Population And Culture
stageGroups.encouragement: Culture round cleared. The final mix gets more demanding.

questions.prompt: Which country is known for producing large amounts of maple syrup?
questions.explanation: Canada is strongly linked with maple syrup production.

questions.prompt: Which country is famous for tulips and windmills?
questions.explanation: The Netherlands is widely associated with tulips and windmills.

questions.prompt: Which European country is famous for fjords?
questions.explanation: Norway is famous for its long, steep-sided fjords.

questions.prompt: Which country is often called the Land of the Rising Sun?
questions.explanation: Japan is often called the Land of the Rising Sun.

questions.prompt: What is the national currency of Japan?
questions.explanation: The yen is the currency of Japan.

questions.prompt: Which country has the largest area in South America?
questions.explanation: Brazil is the largest country in South America by area.

questions.prompt: Which language pair is most widely used across South America?
questions.explanation: Spanish and Portuguese are the most widely used language pair across South America.

questions.prompt: Which country is well known for the Acropolis in Athens?
questions.explanation: The Acropolis is in Athens, Greece.

questions.prompt: Which country is known for the city of Marrakech?
questions.explanation: Marrakech is a major city in Morocco.

stageGroups.title: Hard Geography Mix
stageGroups.encouragement: Strong map work. One final round remains.

questions.prompt: What is the name of the sea between Italy and the Balkans?
questions.explanation: The Adriatic Sea lies between Italy and the western Balkans.

questions.prompt: What country shares Hispaniola with the Dominican Republic?
questions.explanation: Haiti and the Dominican Republic share the island of Hispaniola.

questions.prompt: Which country is bordered by both France and Portugal?
questions.explanation: Spain borders both France and Portugal.

questions.prompt: Which city is located in South America?
questions.explanation: Buenos Aires is in South America.

questions.prompt: What body of water lies between Saudi Arabia and Africa?
questions.explanation: The Red Sea lies between the Arabian Peninsula and northeastern Africa.

questions.prompt: Which desert covers much of northern Africa?
questions.explanation: The Sahara covers much of northern Africa.

questions.prompt: Which country is north of the United States and south of the Arctic Ocean?
questions.explanation: Canada lies north of the United States and reaches the Arctic Ocean.

questions.prompt: Which country is home to the ancient ruins of Angkor Wat?
questions.explanation: Angkor Wat is in Cambodia.

questions.prompt: Which sea is bordered by Turkey, Ukraine, and Georgia?
questions.explanation: The Black Sea is bordered by Turkey, Ukraine, Georgia, and other countries.

questions.prompt: What is the capital of Spain?
questions.explanation: Madrid is the capital of Spain.

questions.prompt: Which country is not in South America?
questions.explanation: Portugal is in Europe; the other countries are in South America.

questions.prompt: A clue says: island country in the Indian Ocean, east of Africa. Which answer fits best?
questions.explanation: Madagascar is an island country in the Indian Ocean east of Africa.

questions.prompt: Which country borders both India and China?
questions.explanation: Nepal borders both India and China.

questions.prompt: Which landmark is on the African continent?
questions.explanation: The Pyramids of Giza are in Egypt, on the African continent.

questions.prompt: Which sea is bordered by Ukraine, Turkey, and Russia?
questions.explanation: The Black Sea is bordered by Ukraine, Turkey, Russia, and other countries.

questions.prompt: Which country is also commonly treated as a continent?
questions.explanation: Australia is both a country and commonly treated as a continent.

questions.prompt: Which river flows through Baghdad?
questions.explanation: The Tigris River flows through Baghdad.

questions.prompt: Which mountain range runs along the western side of South America?
questions.explanation: The Andes run along the western side of South America.
